records.title: Large language model-based multi-agent systems for automated foundation design: router-driven task classification and expert selection framework
records.rationale: Runs an explicit three-way head-to-head of single-agent processing, a designer-checker multi-agent pair, and router-based expert selection across four base models, which is exactly the single-vs-multi contrast RQ2 asks about, but the task domain is geotechnical foundation calculation rather than software engineering and the sample is only 27 cases.

records.title: An LLM-based multi-agent framework for automated reliability analysis of spatially variable soils
records.rationale: Presents a named hierarchical orchestrator-plus-subagent architecture whose self-correction mechanism improves code-execution robustness and whose prompt design affects token and time efficiency, but the target activity is soil reliability analysis and no single-agent configuration is compared.

records.title: Minimizing Response Latency in LLM-Based Agent Systems: A Comprehensive Survey
records.rationale: Decomposes end-to-end agent latency into a four-layer taxonomy with a dedicated layer on mitigating communication and coordination overhead in collaborative agent ensembles, giving structured evidence for the cost and latency penalty side of multi-agent orchestration.

records.title: Agentic AI Modernization: Transforming Institutional Infrastructure Through Orchestrated Multi-Agent LLM Framework
records.rationale: Targets a genuine software engineering activity (COBOL/MUMPS/PL-I legacy code analysis, migration, and validation) with a specialized multi-agent architecture mapped onto institutional governance structures and reports modernization and manual-intervention rates, though its claim that single-agent approaches are inadequate is asserted rather than measured against a single-agent baseline.

records.title: An agent-Based service architecture for smart greenhouses: Telemetry analytics and decision support with RAG-grounded LLM agents
records.rationale: Applies orchestrated LLM-RAG agents to hydroponic greenhouse telemetry and emergency triage; the only comparison reported is GPT-5.2 versus GPT-4o-Mini on domain question answering, not single-agent versus multi-agent, and no software engineering activity is involved.

records.title: Intelligent Site Reliability Engineering: A Multi-agent LLM Framework for Automated Incident Analysis and Root Cause Determination
records.rationale: Operations and incident response is an in-scope SE activity, and the paper measures a hierarchical master-plus-five-specialist architecture against 350 systematically injected failure scenarios using chaos engineering tooling, giving concrete fault-injection methodology and accuracy figures for RQ3's measurement question.

records.title: A Review of Multi-Agent AI Systems for Biological and Clinical Data Analysis
records.rationale: Quantifies an "unreliability tax" of 15-50x higher token consumption for multi-agent systems relative to standalone LLMs and describes cascading amplification of initial hallucinations across the agent collective, which is directly transferable evidence on multi-agent cost and error propagation despite the biomedical setting.

records.title: An Explainable AI Multi-Agent Recommender System for Financial Document Access Control
records.rationale: Reports near-parity between the multi-agent system (83.71%) and the best individual model (84.93%) with unanimous three-agent agreement reaching 92.28%, a useful consensus-versus-parity data point, but the "agents" are fine-tuned classifiers in an ensemble rather than role-specialized agentic LLMs and the domain is financial document classification.

records.title: Multi-Agent AI Framework for Threat Mitigation and Resilience in Machine Learning Systems
records.rationale: The multi-agent RAG system is used as an extraction pipeline over 300 articles and 854 repositories rather than being the object of study, so it contributes ML-lifecycle vulnerability taxonomy background but no evidence on agent coordination or single-versus-multi performance.

records.title: Making waves: A conceptual framework exploring how large language model-based multi-agent systems could reshape water engineering
records.rationale: A speculative perspective piece on hypothetical LLM-MA applications to water distribution and flood management with no empirical results, no software engineering activity, and no single-agent comparison; classic snowball drift into an unrelated application of the same framework family.

records.title: A Critical Review and Evaluation of LLMs for RTL Generation
records.rationale: Combines a 31-study synthesis that classifies multi-agent orchestration as one methodological dimension with a fresh benchmark evaluation showing frontier models under a lightweight reflection loop match or exceed specialized domain pipelines, plus a concrete failure taxonomy (FSM mis-sequencing, handshake drift, blocking/non-blocking misuse) for generated code.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence agents for biological research: a survey
records.rationale: Surveys over 100 studies of agents for clinical analytics, drug design, and multi-omics; the reliability and evaluation challenges it names are generic and it offers no software engineering content and no single-agent versus multi-agent comparison.

records.title: AI Agents vs. Agentic AI: A Conceptual taxonomy, applications and challenges
records.rationale: Its central contribution is precisely the single-agent versus multi-agent collaborative boundary, contrasting modular task-specific AI Agents with Agentic AI built on multi-agent collaboration and persistent memory, and it names coordination failure, brittleness, and emergent behavior as paradigm-specific failure modes relevant to RQ3.

records.title: The Rise of Agentic AI: A Review of Definitions, Frameworks, Architectures, Applications, Evaluation Metrics, and Challenges
records.rationale: Provides a broad 143-study landscape with a classification of qualitative and quantitative evaluation metrics and coordination challenges, but explicitly mixes LLM-based and non-LLM-driven agentic systems and never isolates software engineering or single-versus-multi outcomes.

records.title: Generating Synthetic Behavioral Health Data: A Multi-Agent LLM System
records.rationale: A proof-of-concept cooperative multi-agent system for building smoking-cessation persona simulations; the evaluation is a single illustrative case study in mHealth with no software engineering task, no baseline, and no comparative configuration.

records.title: Large language model-driven multi-agent framework for fault detection and diagnostics of variable air volume boxes
records.rationale: Explicitly benchmarks a Planner/Executor/Reporter role-specialized team against a monolithic LLM baseline and reports gains in task completeness and execution reliability, an on-point single-versus-multi comparison weakened by the HVAC diagnostics domain and a 29-unit case study.

records.title: LLM-Based Human-Agent Collaboration and Interaction Systems: A Survey
records.rationale: Indexed with only an author list rather than a usable abstract; the title indicates a survey of human-agent collaboration and interaction patterns, which bears on human oversight of agentic workflows but shows no software engineering scope or architectural comparison from available metadata.

records.title: A Tri-Stage LLM-Coordinated Framework for Order-Driven Scheduling of Earth Observation Satellite Tasks
records.rationale: Uses an LLM multi-agent framework as a training-free heuristic for an NP-hard satellite scheduling problem, benchmarking against optimization algorithms rather than against a single-agent LLM configuration, with no software engineering activity involved.

records.title: Novice Developers’ Perspectives on Adopting LLMs for Software Development: A Systematic Literature Review
records.rationale: An 80-study SLR firmly inside the SE domain that catalogs tasks, advantages, challenges, and future research needs for novice developers using LLM tooling, but it addresses assistant-style adoption perceptions rather than agent architectures or multi-agent orchestration.

records.title: Towards Engineering Multi-Agent LLMs: A Protocol-Driven Approach
records.rationale: Names under-specification, coordination misalignment, and inappropriate verification as the three core deficiencies of multi-agent LLM systems for SE, then measures failure reduction against the MAST taxonomy across function-level and deployment-level code development plus Python and C/C++ vulnerability detection, answering RQ3 on both mechanism and measurement.

records.title: El Agente: An autonomous agent for quantum chemistry
records.rationale: A hierarchical-memory multi-agent system benchmarked on university quantum chemistry exercises; the in-situ debugging and action trace logging are incidental infrastructure for a natural-science workflow, with no SE task and no single-agent contrast.

records.title: AI agent behavioral science
records.rationale: Argues for systematic behavioral observation and intervention design across individual, multi-agent, and human-agent settings and reframes accountability and interpretability as observable behavioral properties, which is a useful measurement lens but supplies no software engineering evidence or comparative results.

records.title: Developing and Evaluating an LLM-based Agent for ExplorViz Using CopilotKit
records.rationale: A single-agent assistant for program comprehension evaluated in a controlled 11-participant usability study, where deterministic tool-based actions scored 4.82/5 while open-ended agent-driven editing scored only 3.00/5 on expectation match, giving concrete evidence that unconstrained agentic action needs guardrails.

records.title: On the Use of Agentic Coding: An Empirical Study of Pull Requests on GitHub
records.rationale: Measures real-world outcomes of a single agentic coding tool across 567 pull requests in 157 open-source projects, reporting 83.8% merge acceptance with 45.1% still requiring human revision especially for bug fixes and project-specific standards, which is high ecological-validity baseline evidence for what one agent achieves unaided.

records.title: Agentic AI and Large Language Models for Autonomous IoT Cybersecurity: A Systematic Survey, Taxonomy, and Research Roadmap
records.rationale: A PRISMA review of 153 studies whose first taxonomy pillar is explicitly agent architecture as single- versus multi-agent, with consolidated benchmarks and an open-challenge analysis spanning hallucination, prompt-injection robustness, latency, and governance for vulnerability discovery and response.

records.title: Advanced Fault Detection and Diagnosis Exploiting Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Applications
records.rationale: Surveys CNN, RNN, Transformer, and GNN approaches to industrial fault detection with no LLM-based agents anywhere in scope, failing the criterion that the agents must be LLM-based.

records.title: Large Language Models for Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review
records.rationale: The canonical LLM4SE synthesis of 395 articles establishing the SE task taxonomy, dataset practices, and performance optimization and evaluation strategies that later agentic work builds on, though its window closes in January 2024 and it predates the multi-agent comparison question.

records.title: Agentic Business Process Management: A research manifesto
records.rationale: A conceptual manifesto proposing framed autonomy, explainability, conversational actionability, and self-modification as required agent capabilities for organizational process governance; relevant to accountability framing but non-empirical and situated in BPM rather than software engineering.
